source.title: Dictionary Guided Sparse Logit Editing for Reliable Jailbreak Attacks
source.authors: Shuai-Biao Han; Rui-Yang Ni; Zhi-Yu Yi; Chang-Long Li; Perley Xu; Wen-Jie Ruan

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether decoding-time logit interventions can bypass safety behavior, using a different method from compliant-prefixing and other opening-bypass methods.
record.gate_note: The paper tests SIBI, an inference-time sparse logit-editing attack, and reports harmful-compliance attack success rates under multiple conditions. It does not test fine-tuning as the intervention in V1 or V2, aligned-versus-base per-token KL for V3, parameter localization for V5, causes of shallowness for V6, or safety-deepening training for V7. The refusal-mass-by-position result is not the KL measure named in V3. Cited results from prior work are not included.
record.test_reason: SIBI is a decoding-time attack that edits logits to suppress refusal tokens. It reports harmful-compliance ASR on safety-aligned chat models, so it bears on V4 (decoding changes defeat refusal) through a different method than prefilling. It does not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is mostly right. The authors say SIBI exposes shallow alignment and reliance on early-token refusal scaffolds, and that external semantic auditing works better than internal hardening. The positional evidence is qualitative, and the 'shallow alignment' claim is asserted by citing Qi et al. rather than tested.
record.recipe_differences: Uses inference-time sparse pre-softmax logit edits, rather than fine-tuning or compliant-opening prefills; it does not change model weights.
record.method_sensitivity: ASR varies with benchmark, model, attack component, reward schedule, temperature normalization, and defense. The paper reports the strongest temperature sensitivity without normalization and substantially lower ASR under external auditing.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-dictionary probability mass declines steeply over the first response tokens in Llama-2-7B-Chat (qualitative, no values).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-token probability mass is concentrated at the first few generation positions of an aligned model.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2026
record.problems: No uncertainty intervals or significance tests are reported for the ASRs. The main experiments use an automated judge, and the paper reports cyclic sampling and repeated iterations but does not give uncertainty estimates for those results. The reported positional result is qualitative and measures refusal-token mass rather than aligned-versus-base KL.
record.rows_left_out: Table 6's dictionary-size sweep is not extracted: it varies the number of intervention tokens, not the weights or ranks named in V5, and does not test another claim version. Figure 4's per-stem values are not separated because only aggregate SIBI ASR is stated in text; that aggregate is recorded as r57.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples was not tested.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models. Only a qualitative refusal-mass curve is given.
Compliant-token prefilling, adversarial suffix attack tested only as a baseline, and sampling-parameter changes alone as a bypass were not tested.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety. Token dictionaries are not weights.
Causes of shallowness in data or objective were not tested.
No deepening training was tested. The only fine-tuned condition (r22) is a defense check with SFT on 1k refusal pairs.

missing.what: Dictionary-size sweep (k=128 to 1024) with ASR 85.6–95.8 on AdvBench, showing saturation near k≈512
Cross-model dictionary transfer (3.1% drop to Llama-13B, about 7% to Qwen-14B)
Seed-initialization sensitivity: random seeds give 11.2% ASR, versus 95.4% for prototypical seeds

record.verdict_notes: No uncertainty is reported; ASR averages 10 iterations of 30 prompts each. The paper's matched-slice GCG comparison uses 50 prompts. The judge is DeepSeek-R1, but Appendix C.3 names DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, which is inconsistent. Appendix A's retry-until-success policy conflicts with the single-attempt ASR in Appendix E, so main-table ASRs may be inflated. The text mentions 'Qwen3' in the reference list while the models are Qwen-14B-Chat. The study is not one of the claim's original sources.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fine-tuning on harmful examples or measure the effect of such fine-tuning on harmful compliance.
Does not test ordinary or carefully selected benign fine-tuning data.
Does not compare aligned and base models' per-token KL divergence across response positions.

Tests sparse logit edits during decoding, but not compliant-token prefilling, adversarial suffixes as the bypass intervention, or other decoding changes such as sampling-parameter changes as standalone bypasses.
Studies sparse vocabulary-token interventions, not whether a small set of model weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Does not test whether training data or the training objective causes safety behavior to be shallow.
Does not test training intended to distribute safety across response positions or whether such training remains robust.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7B-Chat

conditions.value: refusal stems including “I cannot”, “I apologize”, and “I am unable”

rows.note: The paper reports the aggregate in text; per-stem values are figure-only.
rows.check: A priming condition where refusal stems are forced. The paper reports an average of about 39.6% against GCG's 9.9%. This is the one row that resembles prefilling; it is a weak SIBI result, not a test of compliant prefilling.

relation.reason: The study directly measures harmful-compliance ASR under decoding interventions on aligned models, bearing on V4.

tranche.reason: Sparse inference-time logit editing tests whether decoding interventions bypass refusal, using a different method from compliant-opening prefilling.

source_check.notes: Protocol inconsistencies: Appendix A/Table 8 specifies a 20-failure retry cap, Table 11 specifies three attempts, and Table 14 explicitly reports single attempts; Section 5 names Qwen-14B-Chat while Appendix B names Qwen-14B-Instruct. Section 6.2 explicitly attaches the matched 50-prompt slice to GCG; Section 6.4 describes positional refusal-mass decline, not the aligned/base per-token KL required by V3.

statements.correction: Table 2: AdvBench ASR=95.4% for Llama-2-7B-Chat; 95.8% for Qwen-14B-Chat. Section 5: judge=DeepSeek-R1. Appendix C.3, Table 11: judge=DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B. Abstract: implementation link supplied. Intervention: sparse pre-softmax edits without weight updates.
statements.problem: The SIBI ASRs and logit-editing description match, but the judge attribution omits an internal discrepancy.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SIBI across the main benchmarks and the tested newer instruct/chat models
reader_labels.reason: SIBI yields high harmful-compliance ASRs under decoding-time sparse logit editing (r1-r18, r28, r31, r34, r35-r38, r40-r42, r45-r47, r50, r52, r54).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Component ablations, less effective schedules, temperature settings without normalization, and tested defenses
reader_labels.reason: Attack success is weaker for reward-only intervention, some schedules and unnormalized temperature settings; SFT and logit controls reduce ASR, and external auditing reduces it substantially (r22-r27, r29-r30, r32-r33, r39, r43-r44, r48-r49, r51, r53, r55). Refusal-stem priming also leaves SIBI at approximately 39.6% ASR (r57).
